Commentary.Commentary: First though, the visitors will aim to get through to Tea unscathed. Can they do so? Join us in a while to find out.
A little more than 2 days to go in this Test and a miracle will be needed by Pakistan if they are to salvage something out of this game.
A 100-run stand between Amla and de Kock and another superb stand between Rabada and Quinton have probably batted the touring team out of this Test match.
Pakistan though did have their moments in this innings. They had South Africa at 93 for 5 when their pacers were wreaking havoc.

The Proteas entered this session with a lead of 309 and they had only three wickets in hand. Pakistan would have sensed an opportunity to keep them under 350 but it wasn't meant to be. De Kock and Rabada came out playing their strokes. Especially the former who got a brilliant ton. The latter supported him really well. The two added 79 runs and threatened to take the lead past 400. Shadab Khan though got the centurion and then the last two fell quickly, keeping the Proteas' lead below 400.
The heavy roller is called for from the Pakistan skipper as he walks back to the dressing room. A huge task lies ahead for them as the hosts have set them a huge target of 381.

OUT! Shadab gets the last man. Khan gets his third of the innings. It is a nicely flighted delivery on middle, Olivier tries to defend it off the front foot but gets an outside edge on it as the ball turns away. Sarfraz behind the stumps takes it brilliantly. He picks up his 10th catch of the match as well. South Africa are all out for 303.
Tosses it up on middle, Duanne defends it off the front foot.
Flatter outside off, Olivier lets it go.
The ball has found the edge of the bat. They pick up a single.
Another bumper, Olivier getting a taste of his own medicine. He though is playing it well as he once again ducks under it.
Now comes from around the wicket and bowls it short. Duanne ducks under it.
Another short ball, the batter ducks under it.
Duanne Olivier is the last man in for Proteas.

OUT! In the air... taken! No. 9 goes down as Rabada walks back after playing a handy knock. It is short and angled across the batter. Rabada tries to drag his pull but ends up getting a top edge. Shadab Khan at covers takes an easy catch.
On a length and outside off, Rabada slashes at it but misses.
Gives it a bit of air on middle, Dale blocks it out.
Outside off, DS lets it go.
Tosses it up on off, Dale tries to defend it but the ball spins away beating the outside edge of the bat.
Flighted delivery on middle,Steyn tries to defend it but gets an outside edge and the ball falls just short of the first slip fielder.
Dale Steyn is the new man in.

OUT! De Kock departs. It was a tossed up delivery on middle, de Kock goes for the slog but gets a top edge on it and the ball goes uppishly towards deep square leg. The fielder, Hasan Ali, there takes a good catch in the end. An outstanding and entertaining innings comes to an end. Surely it has to be one of his best innings. He came in when the chips were down, but took the attack to the opposition by playing some brilliant shots. Standing ovation from the dressing room and from the crowd who have come in numbers. Top knock from him.
SIX! Flighted delivery on middle, de Kock goes down in one knee and slogs it over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.
Another play and a miss! Length outside off, KG throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
Back of a length on off, it is kept out.
Slightly short and outside off, Rabada looks to cut but is done in by the extra bounce.
EDGY FOUR! Frustrating this for the visitors! Lands it around off, Rabada tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and races to the third man fence.
Wide outside off, Rabada hangs his bat out and gets beaten.
Back of a length around off, Rabada looks to punch it but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

DRINKS - South Africa pile on the runs. The lead is close to 400 now. It will be interesting to see for how much time they will like to bat on? And Faheem Ashraf is also back onto bowl now after Drinks.
Gives it a bit of air on middle, Kagiso drives it towards mid on for a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle, KR watchfully blocks it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Rabada joining the party now. A tad fuller on off, Rabada drives it straight down the ground and to the boundary.
Quicker and flatter on middle, de Kock works it to the leg side for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good delivery to end the over. On a length on off, Rabada tries to defend it but the shapes away a bit beating the outside edge of the bat.
Wide outside off, Rabada slashes it hard but misses it.
Short outside off, de Kock cuts it through point for a single.
FOUR! Make it two from the over. A tad fuller on middle, Kock whips it through mid on and the ball races away to the fence. He is carnage mode now.
Back of a length on middle, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! SHOT! Fuller on middle, de Kock lofts it over the bowler' head and the ball races away to the boundary.
Drags it short on middle, KR punches it towards point.
A tad short on off, Kagiso watchfully defends it.
Flighted again on middle, Rabada defends it off the front foot.
Slower through the air on leg, Rabada tries to flick it but hits him high on the pads.
Flighted on middle, Rabada defends it off the front foot.
Tosses it up on middle, de Kock works it to the leg side for a single.
Back of a length on off, it is kept out.
Works it around the corner and gets to the other end.
Fuller in length on off, it is eased to mid off.
FOUR! Creamed! Right off the middle, you need not run for those. Full and outside off, de Kock leans into the stroke and carresses it through covers. The ball races away.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. One run added to the total.

EDGED AND DROPPED! Sarfraz, the skipper, is the culprit. He indicates that the ball was too high but that should have been taken. Full on off and it shapes away. De Kock tries to whip it through the leg side, against the movement. The ball takes the outside edge and goes behind. Sarfraz leaps, gets to hands to it but the ball bursts through, rolls towards third man for a single. Everything going South Africa's way here.
A tad fuller on off, KR drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Full and wide down leg, Kagiso tries to sweep it but fails it connect it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

NOT OUT! Missing leg and Rabada survives. We did not see that coming. Tossed up delivery on off, Rabada tries to defend it off the front foot but the ball spins back sharply after pitching and hits him on the pads. The bowler appeals and the umpire raises his finger. Rabada then goes for the review. The replay shows it is missing the stumps.
Rabada is a goner! He has been given out LBW. He has reviewed. Looks out though.
Fuller on off, de Kock drives it towards mid off for a single.
Bowls it full down leg, de Kock still tries to sweep it but misses it.
Full on middle, Rabada drives it straight to the cover fielder.
On a length outside off, Kagiso tries to push it but misses it completely.
Good delivery that, Back of a length on off, Rabada tries to punch it but the ball shapes away after pitching, beating the outside edge of  the bat.
In the channel outside off, Rabada lets it go.
Similar delivery, same result.
Length delivery on middle, Kagiso tucks it around the corner for a single.
Quicker on off, Rabada drives it towards mid on and takes a quick single.
On middle, KR watchfully defends it.
Full on middle, Rabada flicks it to the on side.
Tosses it up on middle, Kagiso tries to flick it but the ball spins back sharply after pitching and hits him high on the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Starts off with a tossed up delivery on middle, de Kock works it to the leg side for a single.
Shadab Khan is brought into the attack.
Full and on the pads, it is clipped through mid-wicket for three.
Outside off, Rabada goes after it but gets beaten.
From around the wicket, he lands it on off, it is kept out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Beaten! Nothing great about the delivery, it is just a poor shot. On a length and outside off, Rabada hangs his bat out, the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Chipper over! On middle, Rabada lofts it over mid on and takes two.

FOUR! Fuller delivery on off, de Kock drives it straight down the ground and to the boundary. Brings up his 4th Test Hundred with that. What a knock from the wicket-keeper. High class innings from him. The team was in a spot of bother when he came in but he played really well and gets a magnificent hundred. Standing ovation from the dressing room and the crowd here.
Back of a length on off, de Kock punches it towards point. He does not get the gap he wanted.
Similar delivery, Quinton watchfully defends it.
On a length on middle, de Kock defends it from within the crease.
Driven through mid-off by the batsman.

Comical stuff out there. It was bowled fuller on middle, de Kock drives it towards the non-striker's end and takes off, the ball hits Rabada in the process as he could not get out of his way in time and then it goes towards leg side. He does not get the single he wanted.
Faheem Ashraf is brought into the attack.
On a length and outside off, Rabada tries to punch it but misses it completely.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total. He moves onto 99.
FOUR! A touch short on off, de Kock cuts it through the point region and the ball races away to the fence. With that boundary he moves onto 98.
Similar delivery, de Kock chops it straight to the point fielder.
Short and wide outside off, de Kock punches it straight to the cover fielder.
A touch short outside off, de Kock cuts it straight to the cover fielder.
Bumper this time on middle, Rabada nicely ducks underneath it.
Fuller on middle, Rabada drives it straight to mid off.
A tad fuller on off, KR watchfully defends it.
Short of a length this time on middle, de Kock pulls it through square leg for a single.
Similar delivery, QdK pushes it towards point.
On a length on off, de Kock defends it by presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length on middle and leg, Rabada tries to flick it but misses it completely and hits him high on the pads.
A touch fuller on off, Kagiso defends it by straight bat.
Full on off, Kagiso defends it off the front foot.
Bangs it short this time on middle, Quinton pulls it towards deep fine leg for a run.
Back of a length on middle, de Kock defends it from within the crease.
LEG BYE! On a length on middle and leg, de Kock tries to flick it but hits him high on the pads and the ball goes towards leg side. The batsmen get a run in the process.
On middle, de Kock defends it off the front foot.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock tries to flick it but gets a leading edge onto it and the ball goes towards off side.
De Kock drives it straight to mid on.
Full on middle, QdK defends it from within the crease.
Back of a length on middle, Rabada tucks it to the leg side for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. 14 of the over.
FOUR! GLORIOUS! A touch fuller on off, de Kock leans forward and drives it firmly through mid off for a boundary. He moves onto 90's now. Nervous 90's for de Kock.
Back of a length on off, Quinton punches it towards point.
FOUR! SHOT! Abbas overpitches and de Kock drives it firmly through cover-point for a boundary. This is high class batting from the wicket-keeper.
A touch short on off, de Kock cuts it through point for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Classy from de Kock. Fraction straight, de Kock gets into position and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. First boundary of the session.
Full delivery attacking the stumps, Rabada watchfully defends it.
On middle, Kagiso defends it with a straight bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on off, de Kock tries to defend it but it hits the inside half of the bat and the ball goes towards leg side. The batsman get a run in the process.

The players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock will take strike. Mohammad Amir will start the proceedings.
.... Day 3, Session 2 ....

South Africa continue to boss the game here, their lead is now over 300 and they still aren't done. Yes, Pakistan have managed to take a couple of wickets but they have also conceded close to a 100 runs in this session The lead is already a big one and South Africa will look to add more after the break as there is still a lot of time left in the game. Also, they will eagerly want de Kock to get to his ton which will be only the second of the series. Pakistan, on the other hand, will look to take the two wickets as quickly as possible and then concentrate on their batting. Join us in a while to see how the second session pans out.

Full on off, KR keeps it out. Sarfraz wants to get in one more over quickly and runs to the other end but the umpire has taken the bails off. The over-rate was quite poor in this session. It's time for Lunch on Day 3!
Back of a length on middle, Kagiso defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Full and wide outside off, Rabada slashes his bat at it and the ball goes through gully and to the boundary. Handy runs for South Africa here.
Back of a length on middle, Rabada defends it from within the crease.
A touch short on off, de Kock cuts it through point for a single.
On a length and on off, Quinton defends it off the back foot.
Full on middle, Rabada defends it off the front foot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Overpitched from Amir, de Kock drives it firmly towards point, but a good fielding from Shan Masood denies him the boundary here.
On middle, Quinton drives it straight to the mid on fielder.
Fraction straight, de Kock flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Fuller on off, de Kock drives it straight to the point fielder.
Length again on off, Rabada is solid in defense.
Lovely bowling! Lands it on off, it slants away. Rabada tries to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Good length outside off, the batter first thinks of playing at it but then lets it be.
Lands it on a length and outside off, left alone.
Length ball again around off, de Kock tries to defend but it goes off the outer half towards point for a run.
Back of a length around off, de Kock defends it on the ground.
Mohammad Abbas on for another burst!
Kagiso Rabada is the new man in.

OUT! There is just no bat involved and it is plumb in front. Amir with the breakthrough! Coming to the delivery, it is a toe-crusher, it also comes back in late. Philander is surprised by the sudden change in length, he tries to keep it out with his bat and pad close. Amir appeals as he feels it has hit the boot first. The umpire agrees and raises the finger. Philander though reviews. The replays show it has hit the toe and returns three reds. Philander has to continue his walk back and he takes a review with him. The visitors are into the bowlers now. Lead - 300!
Vernon Philander has been given out LBW here. He though has reviewed, the only question is, has it hit the bat before hitting the toe?
Similar delivery, VP watchfully blocks it.
Fuller delivery on off, Vernon defends it off the front foot.
Back of a length on off, de Kock punches it towards point for a single. With that the lead goes to 300.
In the channel outside off, QdK shoulder arms to it.
Fuller delivery on off, de Kock defends it with a straight bat.
On the 5th stump line, VP lets it go.
On middle, Vernon pushes it straight to mid off.
FOUR! SHOT! A tad short on off, Philander hangs back and punches it through point for a boundary. Shots like these put Vernon in the all-rounder's bracket.
Fuller again on off, VP drives it straight to the bowler.
A touch short on leg, Philander tries to defend it off the back foot but gets hit high on the pad.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock tucks it to the leg side for a run.
Looks like a change in ball here. The umpires are replacing the old ball with a similar type of ball.
On off, Philander defends it onto the ground.
Attacks the stumps again, Philander gets right behind the line of the delivery and blocks it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good running! This is on the shorter side, the batter goes back and then guides it towards gully for a quick run.
Back of a length on off, de Kock goes back and defends it onto the ground.
A little too wide outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Mohammad Amir is back on.
Drifts on his pads, Philander tries to flick it but is hit on the pads and the ball goes towards the leg side.
Outside off, VP lets it go.
Bangs it short on middle, de Kock pulls it to deep square leg for a single.

EDGED! Just short of the fielder. Fuller delivery outside off, Philander goes hard at it, gets a thick outside edge on it and the ball goes to the first slip fielder. It falls just short of Azhar who goes down low but it drops just in front of his hands. Seems to have hurt his fingers but is fine to continue. The batsmen get a run in the process.
Similar delivery, Vernon is rock solid in defense.
On a length on middle, Philander defends it from within the crease.
Cut him in half there! That lands outside off and comes back in sharply. De Kock goes at it with hard hands, leaving a gap between bat and pad, it sneaks through and goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Length again around off, de Kock covers his off pole and blocks it out.
Good length and on off, de Kock is solid in defense.
Another nice looking pull shot! It is slightly short and on middle, Philander transfers his weight onto the back foot and pulls it all along the ground for a run.
On the fuller side, de Kock looks to punch it straight but it goes off the inner half through square leg and a run is taken.
Back of a length on off, it is guided down to third man, it is a little away from the fielder in the deep. A couple taken.
A tad short on middle and leg, Vernon flicks it to the leg side.
FOUR! Ali bangs it short on middle, Philander pulls it through mid-wicket and the ball races away to the fence. These are important runs for Proteas.
Back of a length on middle, VP defends it from within the crease.
In the channel outside off, Philander lets it go.
Full on off, Vernon defends it with a straight bat.
On a length and on middle, de Kock flicks it to square leg for a single.
A touch short and outside off, Vernon tries to slash it hard but misses it.
Another bouncer from Faheem, Philander does not need to play at those.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
NO BALL! Ashraf oversteps. He bowls a bouncer on middle, Vernon ducks underneath it.
Bangs it short on middle and leg, Quinton pulls it to fine leg for a run.
Strays on his pads, de Kock tucks it straight to the square leg fielder.

Appeal for lbw! A touch short on middle, de Kock is on the back foot trying to defend it but it skids off the deck after pitching and he is hit high on the pads. Faheem appeals but the umpire shakes his head.
Full and wide outside off, Philander tries to slash it hard but misses it completely.
Bouncer this time on middle, Philander ducks underneath it.

Back of a length on middle, Vernon defends it from within the crease.
Fuller on off, Philander defends it off the front foot.
A touch short on middle, de Kock pulls it through fine leg for a single.
Angles it into the off pole, Philander gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
On a length and around off, Philander tries to defend but the ball hits the outer half and goes towards point.
On the shorter side, de Kock this time mistimes his pull towards mid-wicket for a run. The lead is 25 short of 300 now.
A good short one, it is bowled at a good height. De Kock does well though to get on top of the bounce and pull it all along the ground through mid-wicket for a brace.
Fullish and on middle, de Kock strokes it to mid on.
A little too wide outside off, the batter shoulders arms to it.
Vernon Philander walks in at number 8.

OUT! Amla departs! He gets an unplayable delivery! It is on a length on off, Amla tries to defend it off the front foot, unfortunately for him, it hits one of the cracks and takes off. It hits him on his gloves and the ball lobs straight to Sarfraz who takes an easy catch behind the stumps, his 9th in the match. Replays later on show that Amla did try and take one hand off the handle so that the ball does not carry but it was too late by then. A much-needed wicket for the visitors as this 102-run partnership was taking the game away from them. Pakistan would hope this opens the floodgates.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! A touch short on off, Amla hangs back and punches it through cover-point for a boundary. Brings up the 100-run stand as well.
On a length on off, Hashim watchfully defends it.

Back of a length on middle, Quinton defends it off the back foot.
Fuller on off, de Kock drives it straight to mid on.
Muted appeal for lbw. Fuller on leg, de Kock tries to flick it but misses it. Bowler appeal but the umpire is not interested in it.
Good yorker from Ashraf. De Kock at the last moment digs it out. Good bowling from Faheem.
NO BALL! Faheem oversteps. It was bowled outside off, de Kock offers no shot to it.

FOUR! Deftly and deliberately done. On a length outside off this time, Amla waits till the ball reaches him and then just guides this off the outside part of the bat through the gap between slip and gully. Smart batting, adding runs without risks.
On a good length, Hash comes ahead slightly and defends the ball.

On a length outside off, Quinton pushes hard at the ball but it goes off the inside edge towards the square leg region for a single.
Length ball on off, de Kock comes ahead and defends it onto the ground.
Sprays this down the leg side, left alone by QdK.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle, Hashim watchfully defends it.
Good delivery that. On a length and on off, Amla tries to defend it off the back foot but gets beaten to it as the ball just shapes away after pitching.
Fuller on off, HA defends it by presenting the full face of the bat.
In the channel outside off, Hashim shoulders arms to it.
A touch short on off, Amla defends it of the back foot.
FOUR! GORGEOUS! Fuller on off, de Kock leans forward and drives it sweetly through covers for a boundary.
Back of a length on off, Amla punches it through point for a run.

Half century! Fraction straight, de Kock tucks it through square leg for a run. Brings up the 15th Test fifty for Quinton. Quality innings so far and it is come at better than a run-a-ball. He came out when South Africa were slightly in a spot of bother but he still played the way he naturally does. Along with Amla, he has taken South Africa in a very commanding position.
LEG BYE! Drifting on his pads, Amla tries to flick it but the ball hits his pads and goes towards fine leg for a single.
Fuller on off, Hashim defends it off the front foot.
Starts off with a length delivery on middle, de Kock tucks it to the leg side for a single.
Hasan Ali is brought into the attack.
FOUR! Overpitched from Amir. Amla leans forward and drives it firmly through covers for a boundary. Good end to the over for Proteas. The lead touches 250!
Fuller on off, Amla drives it through point for a couple of runs.
Sharp delivery that. Fuller delivery on middle, squares Amla up but the batsman nicely defends it from the front foot.
Fuller on off, Hashim watchfully defends it.
FOUR! Amir bangs it short on middle, Amla hangs back and pulls it through square leg for a boundary.
Fuller on off, Amla drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Fraction straight, Amla nudges it to the leg side for a run and keeps strike for the next over.
Bouncer on middle, HA nicely ducks underneath it.
A touch short on middle, Hashim defends it off the back foot.
Full on off, Amla defends it with a straight bat.
On middle, Quinton works it to the leg side and takes off. Gets an easy single in the end.
WIDE! Goes for the bumper but it is too high and the umpire calls it a wide.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock defends it off the front foot.
Outside off this time, left alone by Hash.

Edged and FOUR! Hashim Amla won't mind though, it brings up his FIFTY! His 41st half century in Tests and a very important one at that. He has looked solid as wickets went down around him and pulled his team out of trouble as he has often done before. Coming to the ball, it was a short of a length ball outside off and Amla pushed at it on the back foot without much feet movement. It took a thick edge and screamed wide of the gully fielder who dived full length to his left but cannot get a hand to it. The ball runs away to the ropes.
Four leg byes! On the pads this time off a length, Amla looks to flick the ball but misses. The ball rolls off the pads and goes fine on the leg side and to the fence.
Kept out towards the off side by Hashim, looks for a quick single but it is not available.
Another back of a length delivery defended from the crease.
Length ball on middle, defended back down on the back foot by Amla.

Fuller on off, Quinton drives it sweetly but straight to the cover fielder.

Fraction straight on this occasion, de Kock flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Brings up the fifty-run stand as well. Very important partnership in the context of the game.
A tad fuller on off, de Kock defends it with a straight bat.
Back of a length outside off, Hashim lets it go.
Fuller delivery on off, Hashim defends it by presenting the full face of the bat.

In the channel just outside off, left alone by Hashim.
On a length on middle, Amla flicks it straight to the square leg fielder.
Length delivery on middle, de Kock tucks it to the on side for a run.
On middle, HA defends it with a straight bat.

On the 5th stump line, Amla lets it go.
Fuller on off, Amla drives it sweetly but straight to the point fielder.

Good delivery that. Full delivery outside off, tempting Quinton to drive. De Kock tries to drive but misses it completely.
Outside off, it has been left alone.

Slightly fuller than the last one, Amla shuffles across and defends it onto the ground.
BEAUTY! Amir lands it on a length around middle, it pitches and slants away. Amla tries to defend but is done in by the away movement. The ball whizzes past the outside edge.

Slight hesitation but they eventually cross for the first run today. Length delivery on off, it comes back in a little. De Kock tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards square leg. Quinton wants a run but Amla is a little hesitant at first, they go for it eventually and complete it with ease.
Mohammad Amir to bowl from the other end.
Full on middle, Amla watchfully defends it. Good start from Abbas.
Touch fuller on middle, Hashim works it to the leg side.

Huge appeal for an lbw! A touch short from Abbas around off, the ball hits one of the cracks and jags back in sharply, Amla is on his crease trying to defend it but misses and it hits him on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. The replay shows it is missing the stumps. Just a reminder, Pakistan have zero reviews left.
Full on off, Hashim defends it by presenting the full face of the bat.
In the channel outside off, Amla lets it go.

The players are out in the middle. Hashim Amla will take strike. Mohammad Abbas will start the proceedings on Day 3.

Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock are at the crease now. They will look to bat as long as possible and push the lead towards 300 and above. As for the visitors, they know that every run added will be a thorn that will come to hurt them later as batting fourth on this pitch is not going to be simple in itself, let alone against the Proteas' pace attack. They'd like to split the current duo and then clean up the tail as soon as possible and hope for the best when they come out to chase. Another action-packed day of Test cricket in store, surely! That has been the template for the series so far and we don't expect anything to go out of line here. Join us as we cover all the action when it unfolds at The Bullring in some time from now.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of this final Test between South Africa and Pakistan at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. This day is usually called the 'moving day' in a Test match but do we need one out here? Every day has been a 'moving day' in this series so far with batting units crumbling and wickets falling thick and fast almost every day. This Test too, like the previous two, looks like won't go the distance, as two innings and a half are already done in two days. Unless we see something spectacular from the remaining batsmen of SA, including the ones at the crease, this game could end pretty soon. It is safe to say that the hosts are ahead as they lead by 212 runs, on a surface that is deteriorating every ball and playing tricks as well. Some stayed really low, some bounced more than normal and some just deviated wildly after hitting wide cracks on Day 2. Day 3 should be similar, if not worse.
... Day 3, Morning Session ...

That's all from us. South Africa are in the driver's seat and with the pitch deteriorating, it's only going to get tough for the touring team. How will they respond? Do join us on Sunday at 1000 local (0800 GMT) for Day 3 to find out. Cheers!

In their second essay, South Africa once again lost their stand-in skipper cheaply which was soon followed by the wicket of Aiden Markram after the Tea break. Faheem Ashraf then bowled a double-wicket maiden to reduce the home team to 45/4 but the pair of Hashim Amla and Temba Bavuma combined for a 48-run stand to disallow Pakistan any opening in their batting order. After the fall of Bavuma's wicket, Quinton de Kock arrived and the run rate suddenly picked up. Pakistan are forced on the back foot here and need wickets in a heap to get any semblance of a chance to avoid the whitewash.

Earlier in the morning, the overnight batting pair for Pakistan presented a stern fight. Aided by some sloppy fielding, they managed to frustrate South Africa for an hour. But then the home team bounced back to create inroads. Sarfraz and Babar produced a counterattacking partnership but the innings fell completely flat on its face post that. Duanne Olivier ran amok with yet another fifer in his short Test career and helped South Africa take a handy 77-run lead.

Yet another day dominated by the bowlers in this Test match. 13 wickets went down in total, making it 25 in the first two days and South Africa have managed to gain an upper hand after swelling their lead to 212 runs.
Amir grunts and slants in a full length ball on off, de Kock strides forward and blocks it back solidly. That will be Stumps on Day 2!
Last ball...
Lands it on a length outside off, Quinton stays back and plays it down to point.
On a length around off, angling down, de Kock tries to flick but fails to middle his shot. It brushes his pads, Amir turns to appeal but nothing doing.
The southpaw has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Doesn't matter if this is the last over, if it's there to be hit, de Kock will go after it. Short and wide outside off, Quinton loves it there and spanks it from the crease through backward point.
Angles in a good length ball on off, de Kock plays it close to his body and defends it to covers.
Three minutes left on the clock. This in all likelihood will be the final over of Day 2. Mohammad Amir to bowl it.
Fullish and on off, Amla decides to defend it from the crease.
Shout for an lbw, not given! Ashraf gets one delivery to nip back into the batsman. Amla fails to keep it out and is hit high on the pads. Too high!

FOUR! Picks the gap! Back of a length delivery around off, Amla goes deep inside the crease to make some room and plays it late. Does well to steer it through the gap between slips and gully for a boundary.
Identical delivery, this time Amla bottom edges his back foot punch towards point.
On a length and outside off, Amla moves across and pushes it out from the bottom half of his bat.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Amla allows it through to the keeper.
Faheem Ashraf is back on.
Drags it short and down the leg side, Quinton nudges it to fine leg for a brace. 9 from the over!

FOUR! Sarfraz is visibly upset with his leggie. This time he has pitched it up, right in the half of the batsman, de Kock drives and strokes it through extra covers. Faheem Ashraf runs after it but the ball wins the race. Lead crosses 200!
A touch short around off, Amla punches it in the gap at covers and crosses for a hesitant single. De Kock later on gestures that he didn't hear the call.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and on middle, de Kock tries to pull but it catches the inside edge and runs to fine leg for a run. Sarfraz is losing patience. Screams - 'Ball aage to kar yaar!' Meaning pitch it up.
Crunched away! Flighted full ball on off, Amla strides forward and drives it past the diving extra cover fielder for a run.
FOUR! Nicely worked away! Too full in length on middle, de Kock whips it through mid-wicket and the tiring legs of Abbas give it the chase from mid on. A boundary results.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Fuller and on off, Amla inside edges his attempted drive through square leg for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, Amla is on the back foot as he offers a straight willow in defense.

Pitches it up and around middle, de Kock slices his drive in the gap at cover-point for a brisk single. The fielder makes a sliding stop, has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Would have been close.
Good length ball on off, de Kock remains inside the crease in defense.
Hasan Ali is back on.
A long hop on middle, pulled in front of square leg for one.
A stifled appeal for an lbw! Spinning down the leg side, de Kock tries to flick but misses. Easily missing the leg pole.
Full and on middle, pushed down the ground off the front foot to mid on.
Miscued! This time Shadab overpitches outside off, de Kock tries to drive but gets an inside edge which rolls to leg gully.

FOUR! Easy pickings! Shadab drops it short and on middle, de Kock picks up the length in a trice, immediately goes deep inside the crease with his pull shot and puts it away behind square leg for a boundary.
Full and flighted on off, pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Good length ball angling into the batsman, de Kock gets back and turns it in front of square leg for a run.
FOUR! Shot! Abbas is on the shorter side with his length, it's wide outside off and de Kock smashes it behind point for a cracking boundary.
Nicely gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it to the off side.
Lands it on a length on off, de Kock stays back and brings his bat down at the last moment in defense.
Angles in a full length ball on off, de Kock gets forward and defends it back.
Good length ball on off, de Kock plays it out from the back foot to gully.
Goes on the back foot and works it with the spin to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Full and off, driven with the spin through covers for a single.
Spin and bounce from around middle! Some purchase here for Shadab. But the length is on the shorter side which gives Amla time to play it out safely from the back foot. He taps it down towards point.
Floated and on middle, de Kock drives it down to long on for one. 100 up for South Africa, lead is 177!
A googly landing full around leg, Quinton leans forward and defends it back.
Flighted leg spinner on off, de Kock gets forward and defends it off the inside edge to square leg.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Forces out a length ball wide of mid off for a run.
FOUR! Brilliant shot! Full and angling into the left-hander, de Kock strides forward with a straight bat and unfurls a stupendous drive down the ground for a boundary.
Abbas pulls out. Reason again - Insects in the eye.
Beauty to beat the bat! Abbas angles in a full ball around off, enticing the drive but it then straightens to beat the outside edge.
Fuller and off, de Kock defends it close to his body by closing the face of his bat.
Abbas runs in from 'round the wicket for the southpaw and angles in a length ball on off. Quinton is on the front foot as he pushes it towards mid off.

Oohhh...nearly sneaks through! A quicker one by Shadab. He hurls it in flat around off at 91 kph, Amla brings his bat down late as he keeps it out off the bottom half of his blade. End of a successful over for Pakistan.
Flatter and outside off, tapped down towards point.
Tossed up ball on middle, de Kock plays it with the spin past leg gully for a run.
Quinton de Kock walks in at number 7. A slip and a leg slip in place.

OUT! A wicket goes down against the run of play and the leggie has done the job for Sarfraz. A flighted leg spinner outside off, Bavuma stays back and has a needless poke inside the line. The ball curls away to catch a thin outside edge and Sarfraz makes no mistake. They appeal and the umpire agrees. The 48-run stand is broken, smiles return in the Pakistan camp but the lead is now 170.
Fuller and on off, driven back off the front foot.
Loopy and full on off, Bavuma presses forward and pushes it with the spin to covers.
On a driving length this time, outside off, Amla is not lured into it.
Full and on off, Amla presents a dead straight bat in defense.
Back of a length ball on off, punched from the crease to mid off.
Oohhh...appreciable movement there but it's after leaving the batsman. A length ball outside off, Amla moves across the stumps and shoulders arms. Probably hit a crack there.
Targets the off stump with a length delivery, Amla shuffles across and defends it back.
Starts his spell with a good length ball on middle and leg, Bavuma moves inside the line and glances it down to long leg for a run.
Mohammad Abbas to have another go with the ball. He has a wicket to his name in this innings.
Full and floated on off, Amla prods forward and blocks it to the off side.
A touch short and spinning away from outside off, Bavuma hangs back and punches it through covers for a run. The stand moves to 47!
Flighted and outside off, left alone.
Quicker, flatter and shorter on middle, Bavuma moves back and defends it to the bowler.
FOUR! Smart batting! A loopy full ball around off, Bavuma goes down and across before nailing his sweep shot in front of square leg for a glorious boundary.
The batsman pulls out. Reason - Insects.
A leg spinner on the shorter side, Amla waits for it to spin away and then forces it past the right side of the diving point fielder for a single.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length delivery wide outside off, Bavuma lets it be. So far, this pair has attacked 20 percent of deliveries, blocked 45 percent of balls while left alone percent is 35. Fine approach.
A length ball on off, angling in, Temba offers a straight bat in defense but gets an inside edge onto his boots.
Good length ball outside off, left alone with ease by Temba.

FOUR! Quality shot! Amir overpitches around off, Bavuma confidently strides forward and caresses his drive through cover-point for a delightful boundary. Lead moves to 163 and this partnership is now 41!
Amir speeds in from 'round the wicket and serves a length delivery outside off, Temba has nothing to do with it.
Hashim has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A muted appeal for an lbw! Tossed up ball on off, probably a flipper, Amla draws forward in defense but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Presses forward to a full ball and blocks it safely.
The length is again short, it's around off, Amla goes back and turns it to mid-wicket.
Flatter and shorter on off, Amla punches from the crease to extra cover.
Full and flighted outside off, Bavuma strides forward and drives it through covers for a run.
Shadab Khan into the act now.
Switches to over the wicket and delivers a length ball on middle. Amla works it off his pads to the on side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Amir lets out a grunt and spears in a full ball on off, Amla calmly defends it back.
Good stop, Babar! Back of a length delivery outside off, Amla punches it from the back foot and Azam does well at gully to stop the ball on one bounce.
Now Amir gets a fly in his eye. He pulls out in his delivery stride and Imam is helping him out.
Angles in on off, Amla presents a straight bat and defends it to the off solidly.
Beaten! A hint of reverse there. The angle is quite difficult to deal. Amir angles in a length ball around off and it nips away with the shine. Amla pushes inside the line and misses.
Amir speeds in from 'round the wicket and angles in a length ball on middle, Amla turns it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Faheem bowling with good accuracy. Lands a length ball just around off, Bavuma shoulders arms.
A little short and outside off, TB has an easy leave.
Faheem Ashraf tries rushing through here but Temba Bavuma is not ready. He stops the bowler midway.
Digs in a short ball this time, around off, Bavuma sways away from the line.
Yet another delivery in the region just outside off, Bavuma shoulders arms.
Fine leave. Full and just around off, straightening from there, Bavuma confidently plants his front leg forward and then allows it through. Very assured.
FOUR! Good length delivery just around off, Bavuma delays his shot off the back foot just a bit and then steers it through point for a boundary. Fine timing and placement!
Length ball on off, Amla punches it to covers where the fielder stops it and tries to back flick it onto the stumps at the non-striker's end. Nothing doing.
Angles in a length ball on off, Amla gets forward in defense and takes his bottom hand off the handle in the process. It goes off the outer half and rolls to point this time.
Amla has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Edgy! Amir puts it outside off and Amla feels for it. Gets a soft outside edge and it rolls in front of the slip cordon.
Not in full control of this shot but will get three runs. Full and around off, angling away, Bavuma tries driving through the line but it takes the outside half of his blade and races past point.
Serves a length ball on the pads, it's tickled through square leg for an easy run.
Full and on off, Bavuma gets forward to push it towards point. Looks for a run initially but it's not on.
A touch short and around off, moving back in a bit, Bavuma knows where his off stump is and makes a sensible leave.
Identical to the last delivery but this one is a bit angled in. Bavuma once again shows no interest in chasing it.
Fine delivery but it's not close enough to the off pole to pose any threat. Temba takes his front leg forward to cover the line and then lets it through to the keeper.
Angling into the right-hander, on a fuller length, Bavuma leans forward and defends it with gentle hands to point.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, Bavuma makes an easy leave.

Drinks break in this extended session. Pakistan have managed to pick up three important wickets but runs have also been given. 48 runs in 12 overs at four runs per over. South Africa are batting with Amla and Bavuma at the crease but even they'd know that they can't afford to lose any more quickly as they lower order might open up to the threat of the Pakistan pacers. Let's see what's in store for the last hour and a little more of play today.
Short length ball outside off, Amla punches it towards cover where Shadab moves to his left and makes a tumbling stop.
Another bouncer! Amla ducks under it and evades the ball.
On the pads, worked away to square leg by Temba for a single. The lead is now 150!
Bouncer! A good short delivery on middle and leg. Bavuma tries to pull but it gets big on him and it goes above his bat. Lucky not to have feathered that on its way to Sarfraz.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Temba rides the bounce and defends the ball onto the ground.
Left alone pretty late outside off by Bavuma.

FOUR! Amla has really played some pleasing shots today! This one is fuller on middle and Hashim walks into the drive and pushes it right back down the ground. It is all timing and nothing else as it reaches the rope easily.

Much better from Ashraf this time, gets it back on a length on off stump. The ball goes off the inside half and towards square leg. Bavuma, who was looking for a single, is sent back by his bearded partner.

FOUR! Short and wide! Asking for trouble. Amla does not approve of that delivery and dispatches it away behind point once more for an easy boundary. Loose from Pakistan, might be their first poor ball in some time but every run is important here.
Fuller length ball on off, kept out by HA coming forward.
The crowd enjoying itself here on a Saturday afternoon, lots of jumping and dancing going on. Lovely to see.
Length ball outside off, defended from within the crease.
Short of a length ball on middle, Bavuma rocks back and pulls it away to deep square leg for a single.
Bavuma flicks this one off his pads to the leg side and picks up a single to retain strike.
Kept out on the off side by Temba.

On the pads, worked away by the veteran batsman towards the leg side for a single. Temba Bavuma wanted a second but is sent back in the end by his partner. Was also lazy in getting back as the fielder has a shy at the striker's end. Could have been interesting if he had hit the stumps.
A good length ball on top of off stump, defended back down the ground.
The flies and moths are causing huge problems here. Hashim Amla has pulled out when Amir was in his delivery stride and this is not helping anyone's cause.
This one is on a length and leg stump line, Hash pushes it towards mid-wicket off the back foot.
FOUR! Cut away! A little gift from Mohammad Amir on his return. Hurls this outside off on a length and gentle pace, Amla rocks back and cuts it away behind point. No fielder in the deep to stop it.
Mohammad Amir is back for another burst.
A delivery around off, once again there to be driven. But this time TB has no intention to repeat his last shot. Just shoulders arms and ends the over.
Good shot. Ashraf pitches it up and outside off, Bavuma leans forward and pierces the off side field with a well-timed cover drive. It's chased down in the deep and the batsmen take a couple of runs.
Bowling to a good line here, Faheem. Just putting it on a length and just outside off, playing on Temba's patience. Left alone.
Hurls a length ball outside off, a good leave again by the little batsman.
The line is straight on this occasion and Temba closes the face of his bat to play it towards mid-wicket.
Good leave. On a length and outside off, moving back in a bit with the shine, Bavuma covers his stumps and shoulders arms.

NOT OUT! There is a massive inside edge that is spotted on the first replay itself and the decision has to be overturned here. On a length and the ball seems to have skid on after landing, Amla looked to flick it away but missed to get hit on the pads. Hasan Ali appeals and the umpire raises his finger almost instantly. Hashim takes the referral and the replays find the involvement of his bat. It is quite remarkable how he could miss that inside edge as it was quite thick, maybe the insects caused a distraction. Amla would thank the Almighty for DRS. Would have been a terrible way to get out when you are desperately trying to get back into form, and with your team in a tricky position.

Review time... Hashim Amla has been adjudged out by the umpire but he has immediately reviewed. Looked like a massive deflection from the bat. Just have to wait for the replays to roll in for overturning the decision.
FOUR! Yet again! This time off the front foot. Fuller one outside off, Amla comes ahead and pushes this in the gap wide of mid off. Such a smooth shot with amazing timing. No stopping those.

FOUR! 'Beauty! Amla textbook' quips the on-air commentator. Short length ball outside off, Hashim rocks back and offers a back foot punch to this one. It rolls away wide of point and to the fence. A purist's delight. 50 up for South Africa.
Delivered outside off on a length, left alone by Amla.
Seems like Hasan Ali wants something from the dressing room. Yes indeed, sunglasses. Wears it and will continue bowling, quite a good one for the shutterbugs this.
On the pads and on a length this time, flicked away through mid-wicket by Amla. A couple taken.

Beaten all ends up! This one seems to have taken off from a crack. Puts this on a length and yes, it goes off a wide crack. The ball takes a different route to the one it was coming at and Amla has no answer to that. Beats his outside edge. The pitch is worsening with every passing second.
Fullish and on off, angling in, Bavuma lunges and defends it watchfully. A double-wicket maiden for the second time on Day 2.
Temba Bavuma is the new batsman.

OUT! Are we in for another collapse? Things happening again. This one stays a touch low after landing on a good length around off. The ball shapes back in as well to Hamza's bad luck. He tries to work it around but it goes under his blade and raps him on the pads. Ashraf turns to appeal and the finger has gone up. Zubayr walks without troubling the scorers. No need to review that. A good period of play for Pakistan continues but they need to keep chipping away at the wickets to stay in the hunt.
Ouch! That's a painful welcome for the newbie. Faheem delivers it on a length around off and it jags back in sharply. Hamza tries to defend but misses and takes a blow inside his groin region.
Zubayr Hamza walks in at number 5.

OUT! I can't believe I am saying this but Pakistan's slip catching has been better than South Africa's in this game. An inspired bowling change this, Ashraf has done the trick in his 3rd ball itself. Bowls this one on a length outside off, Theunis de Bruyn looks to drive this away from his body without foot movement. The ball takes a thick outside edge and flies towards Asad Shafiq at second slip who takes a really smart catch. Good passage of play for Pakistan after Tea this, fighting their way back. The lead is 122 now.
Short of a length ball outside off, punched to the cover region by the batsman this time.
On a length on top of middle, punched back down the ground by de Bruyn.
Faheem Ashraf is now into the attack.
FOUR! A bit aerial but wide of the point fielder. Fuller in length outside off, Hashim Amla leans into the square drive and places it nicely to fetch a boundary for himself.

MISSING LEG! Poor review. Pakistan have none left now. Hasan delivers a length ball and it reverses back into Amla, following the shine. The line is on middle and leg and it's further tailing down. Hashim fails to work it around and is thudded on the pads. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. Hasan is confident and Sarfraz backs his bowler. Takes the DRS only to find out that Hasan Ali's assumption was wrong.

Review time... Hashim Amla has been struck on the pads and Hasan Ali has told his skipper to take this one upstairs. It looks like it was going down leg to the naked eye but lets wait for the replays.
The bowler pulls out this time. Hasan Ali was running through to bowl but there were insects in his way and one seems to have gone up his nostril. He pulls out waving his arms all along the way.
Very full on middle, the batsman drives it towards mid on, on the front foot.
This is in line with the stumps but Hashim brings his bat well in front on this occasion to keep this out.

A small appeal but turned down by the umpire. Bowls this on a length outside off, Amla takes a big stride ahead to defend. The ball hits the pad and bat at the same time. Ali appeals but the umpire says no. The impact was well outside off, even if there was no inside edge.
Good ball! On a length outside off, Amla tries to defend coming ahead but pulls out of the shot in the last moment.
Put well outside leg this time by Abbas, de Bruyn leaves it alone as he shadow practices his flick.
Fuller one outside off, TdB gets ahead and drives this but it goes straight to cover.
Fuller one on middle and leg, pushed away to mid-wicket after coming ahead by Theunis.
Length ball outside off, pushed away to covers with soft hands.

The batsman has pulled out yet again. This time, a fly has come in the face of Theunis who backs away as the bowler was running in. It is causing us to lose valuable minutes. Everyone on the field is seen swaying his arms to shoo away the irritating insects.

FOUR! Shot! Amazing timing and control from de Bruyn. A length ball outside off, not much wrong with the delivery but a lovely piece of batting from Theunis. Not much foot movement but just uses his strong hands to push this through the gap wide of mid off. The ball beats the infield and races away.
Good length ball outside off, left alone by Theunis.
Azhar Ali is off! He has not caught a catch but he has caught a fly in his left eye. He is in the dugout, taking someone's help in getting that fly out.
Length ball on middle and off, defended with soft hands by the batsman.

FOUR! Terrific shot! A Hashim Amla special cover drive. Fuller outside off, in fact a half-volley but still had to be put away. And that's what is done, as Amla takes a big stride ahead and crunches it through the covers.
A length ball on off, keeps a tad low. Amla adjusts well as he flicks it towards mid on.
Slightly fuller length this time, Hashim comes ahead and keeps the ball out.
Length ball outside off, defended onto the ground once more.
Mohammad Abbas is getting his shoulders massaged near the boundary line. It is turning into a full body massage as he is spotted lying down now.
Fuller length ball outside off, driven towards a wide mid on fielder. A quick single is taken as the fielder is lazy on the ball. Poor from Pakistan, can't afford to be this loose.
Left alone outside off to end the over.
Length ball on off and shapes away, Hash covers the swing and defends.
Hurls this down the leg stump line, Amla swivels and tries to pull it away but fails to make connection with the ball.
The batsman pulls out this time. Seems a moth came in his line of vision. Getting really irritating now.
This one is on length and holds its line after landing outside off. Hashim judges the line and lets it go through.
Peach! The ball was on a length and shapes away really late after landing. Amla was trying to defend the ball from the crease and plays inside the line. Lucky not to get a nick there. Lovely ball.
A short leg fielder with a helmet comes into position now.
Length ball on the off stump line, defended back from the crease by Amla.
Length ball wide outside off, Theunis cuts this away through the covers. Imam gives the chase and stops it inside the boundary. A couple taken by the batsmen.
Bouncer on middle, too high and de Bruyn just stays under the ball and lets it go.
The mosquito-repellant spray is out once more. The umpires and de Bruyn using it. Slight stoppage in play due to that.
Length ball outside off, defended back onto the ground from the crease.
Pitches it up and outside off, Theunis takes a stride forward to cover the line as he leaves it alone.
Targets the off stump with a length ball, de Bruyn stays on the back foot in defense.
Appreciable movement on this one. But the line is too straight and it tails down to catch Amla on the pads as he fails to flick. It clips his pads and runs behind for a leg bye.
Fullish and on off, once again Theunis offers a straight blade in defense. Good start to the session for Pakistan.
Angles in a length ball on off, de Bruyn gets forward with a straight bat and defends it to the off side.
Theunis de Bruyn is the new batsman at number 4.

OUT! A brilliant take from Sarfraz behind the wickets, diving full length to his right. Just two balls before, it was mentioned that Abbas is always accurate and McGrath-like with his lines and lengths. He bowls a third consecutive ball outside off and shapes this slightly away. Aiden Markram tries to push at it with not much foot movement and he only manages to get a healthy edge. The ball goes towards first slip, wouldn't have carried to Azhar Ali, Sarfraz senses that and really does well to dive to his right to pouch it. Pakistan have their second wicket of the innings and this could give them a really good boost. Markram departs after looking decent during his stay at the crease. This passage of play will be a very interesting one now if their bowlers get their tails up!
Another good length ball outside off, pushed away towards cover-point by the batsman.
Much better on the line outside off, defended back to the bowler.

FOUR! What a way to start proceedings. Overpitched on middle and leg, easy pickings for a batsman of Markram's caliber. This was very unlike Abbas who usually is super accurate. Not an ideal start for Pakistan, can't afford half-volleys like these, the game can slip away from them in no time.
The players and the umpires are back out in the middle for the final session of play. Mohammad Abbas has the ball in hand. Aiden Markram to face him, Amla at the other end.
... Day 2, Third Session ...

An interesting but funny development during this session was when we had uninvited visitors, a lots of moths and flies. It has caused us to lose precious time and 39 overs remain to be bowled in the day. Whether it will be completed or not remains to be seen, but what we do know is that it is going to be a really fun final session if things continue the same way. Will the Proteas build a massive lead or can the Pakistan bowling attack produce some magic? Wait with us to find out, as we bring you the post-Tea session in a little time.

An incredibly fast-moving session, not in terms of overs bowled but by the number of wickets lost. 22.4 overs bowled, 6 wickets lost. Five by the visitors and then one of Dean Elgar in South Africa's second dig. The hosts go into the break effectively 102/1 and one can safely say they are ahead in the game. Having said that, Pakistan are fighting hard and a good burst of bowling where a clump of wickets could be taken, should bring them back in the game. Coming to session that passed though, it started off in quick fashion as Sarfraz and Babar added runs at a great clip. But once that stand was broken, it was quick work from the SA pacers as they bundled out Pakistan for a measly 185. They then have come out to bat and added 25 in 8 overs with the loss of their skipper.
Left alone outside off, that will also be TEA ON DAY 2!
A length ball outside off, defended by the batsman with a straight bat.

A ripper! This has exploded off a crack and deviated away late. Lands this on a length outside off, Amla was ahead to defend but the movement in the end squared him up and the ball goes through to the keeper. Lucky not to have got an edge on that.
Slightly pushes the length up, the batsman comes ahead and defends on his front foot.
Outside off this time, left alone by Hash.
A good ball first up. On a length and top of middle and off, defended by Amla from the crease.
Hasan Ali into the attack now.
A good leave outside off as the ball goes along with the angle and through to the keeper.
Slightly fuller this time outside off, he pushes it towards point coming on the front foot.
Another short length ball on top of middle, pushed back down towards the bowler by Markram.
Length ball outside off, the batsman is content in blocking it out.
A short cover in position now.
Another length delivery that Aiden defends the ball on his back foot.
A good length ball on middle, Markram defends from within the crease.
Length ball on middle, defended towards mid-wicket with soft hands.

Shout for an lbw! Length ball on off stump and seems to have jagged in a bit after landing. Amla was pushing forward to defend but the ball beats him as he plays outside the line. The ball rapped him on the pads and a loud appeal followed, mostly from Abbas. The umpire says no and it seemed a good decision as it looked like the impact was outside off. Sarfraz doesn't think about reviewing it, a good call in the end as replays show that the impact indeed was outside off.
Length ball outside off, Amla defends solidly.
Fuller one outside off, the batsman defends it coming a little forward.
Outside off on a length, Hashim takes a stride ahead as he leaves this delivery well.
Length ball on off, Amla covers the swing and defends watchfully towards mid on.
Mohammad Abbas pulls out of the delivery at the last moment. Seems like a moth has come in his face.
Good work from Amir. Bowls a heavy delivery, on a length around leg, Markram tries working it on the leg side but misses.
A touch short around leg, Amla glances it off his hips to deep square leg for a run. He is off the mark.
A length ball angling away around off, Amla prods forward in defense.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Good length ball on off, Amla defends it off his back foot.
Hashim Amla walks in at number 3, replacing his skipper.

OUT! There is an inside edge. This time Pakistan are successful with the use of DRS. Amir comes up with a brilliant delivery. He lands it on a good length around off and gets it to shape back in with some extra bounce. Elgar tries to defend it but it appears that he has failed to put bat on ball. It strikes him high on the back leg and lobs to the keeper. A huge appeal follows but the umpire stays put. Amir is convinced here (we're not sure, about lbw or inside edge) and suggests his skipper to take the review. Sarfraz obliges. The replays roll in and the Ultra Edge detects some wood. The decision is reversed and Pakistan earn their first wicket. 10 runs in total in this Test match as the stand-in skipper for Elgar. Pressure?

Another review... Not quite sure whether it is for an LBW or for caught behind. Looked like the ball missed everything and got the thigh pad as it goes to the keeper. Loud appeal from everyone and Amir persuades his skipper to go upstairs as he felt there was some bat on it. Sarfraz acknowledges it.
Angling into the batsman, on a length around middle, Markram works it off his pads to the leg side.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Shot! Back of a length delivery outside off, Markram rises on his back foot and packs a punch through covers for a crackling boundary. Lead crosses 100 now!
On a length around off, defended off the back foot.

INSIDE EDGE! No need to see further. Pakistan lose a review. A length ball landing around off and shaping back in. Markram gets half-forward to defend but misses and is rapped on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal for an lbw. Sarfraz has a chat with his bowler and decides to review it. Rest is history.

Review time... An LBW appeal against Markram has been turned down by umpire S Ravi. Looks like the impact was outside off to the naked eye, might be umpire's call. Let's wait what the replays have to say.
Gentle delivery, on a length and outside off, an easy leave for Markram.
Another ball that has been left alone by Elgar outside his off stump.
Well outside off this time, left alone by the SA skipper.

Lovely looking shot from Markram. On a length from Amir and on off stump, Aiden stands tall and punches it through the covers. The mid off fielder gives chase and manages to just about to keep it in with a lovely diving effort. Saves a run for his team. The replays show it is a clean stop.
The sun is shining again after hiding behind the clouds for a brief period.
Good ball from Amir! On a length outside off, holds its line and Markram, who was ahead to defend, is beaten on the outside.
Hurls this one at the pads, Elgar works it away to deep square leg for a single.
Outside off on a length, left alone by the batsman.

Oh dear, Mohammad Amir! The poor boy is struggling big time, not with his fitness, not with the landing of his ball, he is struggling while fighting with moths. Plenty of flies all over the shirt of umpire S Ravi. We have unwanted visitors here. It's a take over at the Wanderers Stadium. Out comes the spray to fight the battle! Umpire Ravi is seen applying some cream on his body to repel the flies. We've a halt in play once again.

FOUR! Edged this time, but the ball goes all along the ground away from the third slip fielder for a boundary. Length ball outside off, Aiden Markram tries to push the ball away but it goes off the outside edge. The batsman does well to remove his bottom hand. It goes along the ground and Shadab dives to his right to stop the ball but fails to do so. A boundary results. 12 runs off Abbas' first over, an expensive start.

Plenty of flies and moths on the field. Hasan Ali is fighting the battle at covers with his hat. Azhar Ali doing the same at slips. In fact, all the Pakistan players are trying to swat the flies away with their caps. Quite funny. Slight halt in play.
Length ball at the pads, worked through mid-wicket by the batsman for a couple of runs.
Sprays this one down the leg side and the movement takes it even further. Sarfraz fails to collect it properly and a couple of byes are taken as the ball runs to fine leg.
Play and a miss! On a length outside off, Markram looks to cut this one but is beaten by the extra bounce.

FOUR! Punches the second ball he faces for a boundary though. On a length outside off, Aiden Markram takes a small step ahead and punches this one through the covers. Finds the gap easily and the ball runs to the fence.
Outside off to start with, Markram leaves the ball nice and early.
Mohammad Abbas to share the new ball.
Good length delivery outside off, Elgar allows it through to end the over.
A little bit of width outside off, Elgar plays it down from the crease to point.

FOUR! Nicely done in the end! Amir angles in a length ball around off, staying a bit low, Elgar brings down an angled bat and gets it away off the lower half of his blade. It races past the diving third slip fielder for a boundary. Soft hands, the key.
Make it three leaves in a row from Elgar.
Yet another delivery in the zone outside off, Dean shoulders arms. The conditions have turned overcast all of a sudden and should assist the Pakistan seamers.
Starts with a good length delivery in the channel outside off, Elgar allows it  through watchfully.
